requirements.subject: ent:setverdict-operation
requirements.canonical: The local verdict IS set with the `setverdict` operation.
requirements.original: The local verdict is set with the setverdict operation.

requirements.subject: ent:setverdict-operation
requirements.canonical: The `setverdict` operation has the syntax `setverdict ( SingleExpression { , ( FreeText | TemplateInstance ) } )`, i.e. a verdict expression followed by zero or more free text or template instance arguments.
requirements.original: setverdict "(" SingleExpression { "," ( FreeText | TemplateInstance ) } ")"

requirements.subject: ent:setverdict-operation
requirements.canonical: The `setverdict` operation IS changing the value of the local verdict.
requirements.original: The value of the local verdict is changed with the setverdict operation.

requirements.subject: ent:setverdict-operation
requirements.canonical: The change of the local verdict by the `setverdict` operation SHALL follow the overwriting rules of table 30.
requirements.original: The effect of this change shall follow the overwriting rules listed in table 30.

requirements.subject: ent:setverdict-operation
requirements.canonical: A `setverdict` operation MAY have optional FreeText or TemplateInstance arguments providing information that explains the reasons for assigning the verdict.
requirements.original: The optional parameters allow to provide information that explain the reasons for assigning the verdict.

ambiguity.issue: 'optional parameters' refers to the optional FreeText/TemplateInstance arguments (actual parameters) of setverdict.

requirements.subject: ent:setverdict-operation
requirements.canonical: The information given in the optional arguments of a `setverdict` operation IS composed into a single string.
requirements.original: This information is composed to a string and stored in an implicit charstring variable.

ambiguity.issue: The composition rule is not stated; chose reading 1 (as for log, cf. example 2 'Value received: 5').
readings: The optional arguments ARE concatenated without separators, each converted to text as the log statement does.
The optional arguments ARE composed into a string using an implementation-dependent format.

requirements.subject: ent:implicit-charstring-variable
requirements.canonical: The string composed from the optional arguments of a `setverdict` operation IS stored in the implicit charstring variable of the test component.
requirements.original: This information is composed to a string and stored in an implicit charstring variable.

requirements.subject: ent:local-verdict
requirements.canonical: On termination of a test component, the actual local verdict IS logged together with the implicit charstring variable.
requirements.original: On termination of the test component, the actual local verdict is logged together with the implicit charstring variable.

requirements.subject: ent:setverdict-operation
requirements.canonical: The optional arguments of a `setverdict` operation SHALL obey the same rules and restrictions as the parameters of the `log` statement.
requirements.original: Since the optional parameters can be seen as log information, the same rules and restrictions as for the parameters of the log statement (clause 19.11) apply.

requirements.subject: ent:implicit-charstring-variable
requirements.condition: the local verdict is assigned a value different from the previous one
requirements.canonical: Whenever a `setverdict` operation overwrites the local verdict of a test component with a value different from the previous one, the implicit charstring variable IS overwritten.
requirements.original: As the result of the setverdict operation, the implicit charstring variable is overwritten whenever the local verdict of a test component is overwritten (i.e. a new value, which is different to the previous one is assigned to it).

requirements.subject: ent:implicit-charstring-variable
requirements.condition: the local verdict value does not change
requirements.canonical: If a `setverdict` operation does not change the value of the local verdict, the implicit charstring variable IS NOT overwritten.
requirements.original: As the result of the setverdict operation, the implicit charstring variable is overwritten whenever the local verdict of a test component is overwritten (i.e. a new value, which is different to the previous one is assigned to it).

requirements.subject: ent:implicit-charstring-variable
requirements.condition: setverdict has only a verdict argument and changes the local verdict
requirements.canonical: A `setverdict` operation with only a verdict argument that overwrites the current local verdict IS clearing the implicit charstring variable, so that previously stored information is lost.
requirements.original: A setverdict operation with a verdict only that overwrites the current local verdict, will also clear the implicit charstring variable. This means previously stored information gets lost.

requirements.subject: ent:setverdict-operation
requirements.canonical: The `setverdict` operation SHALL only be used with the values `pass`, `fail`, `inconc` and `none`.
requirements.original: a) The setverdict operation shall only be used with the values pass, fail, inconc and none.

requirements.subject: ent:setverdict-operation
requirements.canonical: The `setverdict` operation SHALL NOT be used to assign the value `error`.
requirements.original: It shall not be used to assign the value error, this is set by the test system only to indicate runtime errors.

requirements.subject: ent:error-verdict
requirements.canonical: The `error` verdict IS set only by the test system to indicate runtime errors.
requirements.original: It shall not be used to assign the value error, this is set by the test system only to indicate runtime errors.

requirements.subject: ent:single-expression
requirements.canonical: The SingleExpression of a `setverdict` operation SHALL resolve to a value of type `verdicttype`.
requirements.original: b) _SingleExpression shall resolve to a value of type verdict._

requirements.subject: ent:setverdict-operation
requirements.canonical: The FreeText and TemplateInstance arguments of a `setverdict` operation SHALL obey the same rules and restrictions as the parameters of the `log` statement.
requirements.original: c) For FreeText and TemplateInstance, the same rules and restrictions apply as for the parameters of the log statement.

requirements.subject: ent:getverdict-operation
requirements.canonical: The value of the local verdict MAY be retrieved using the `getverdict` operation.
requirements.original: The value of the local verdict may be retrieved using the getverdict operation.

requirements.subject: ent:getverdict-operation
requirements.canonical: The `getverdict` operation has the syntax `getverdict` (the keyword alone, without parentheses or arguments).
requirements.original: getverdict

requirements.subject: ent:getverdict-operation
requirements.canonical: The `getverdict` operation IS returning the actual value of the local verdict as a `verdicttype` value.
requirements.original: The getverdict operation returns the actual value of the local verdict.
